critic.title: Lighter auth token reaches the committed snapshot, /api/state, the web UI and CLI status through the ACTIVE_ORDERS_UNAVAILABLE error text
critic.requirement: Handoff/spec forbid secrets in logs, API or UI. Spec §11: "Секреты и auth token не выводятся". NG-UI-001 forbids secrets in API responses. NG-UI-002 says the drill-down and audit history must contain no secrets.
critic.failure_scenario:
1. LighterAuth.rest_authenticate (lighter_perpetual_auth.py:26) always adds `auth=<token>` to the query of authenticated GETs. fetch_active_orders (lighter_perpetual_derivative.py, is_auth_required=True) is one of them.
2. Lighter or a proxy/CDN answers accountActiveOrders with a status below 400 and a Content-Type that is not JSON, text/plain or text/html. Examples: an empty 200/204 with no Content-Type (aiohttp reports it as application/octet-stream), or text/xml.
3. Hummingbot's RESTResponse.json() then calls aiohttp's json(), which raises aiohttp.ContentTypeError. Its str() is `200, message='Attempt to decode JSON ...', url='https://.../accountActiveOrders?account_index=..&market_id=..&auth=<TOKEN>'`.
4. ContentTypeError is not an IOError, so it passes through _api_request unchanged. LighterExchangePort.active_orders (lighter_port.py:348) catches only LighterHistoryResponseError, so it passes through there too.
5. NeutralGridEngine._refresh_account catches it at engine.py:1349-1351: `self._error("ACTIVE_ORDERS_UNAVAILABLE", f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", now)`. No redaction is applied.
6. snapshot.build_summary copies engine.errors into the snapshot (snapshot.py:224). The snapshot is committed to SQLite and served by /api/state (server.py:179 `errors`). app.js renderErrors shows it in the UI. format_status prints the last 5 errors in the CLI `status` (snapshot.py:329-330). executor.get_custom_info also exposes the snapshot to the V2 controller.
The token grants read access to the account's private orders and trades for about 10 minutes (DEFAULT_AUTH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_SECONDS). The copy in the SQLite snapshot rows is persisted indefinitely.
Other history paths only record type(exc).__name__: the scanner's page_fetch_error and the port's submit/cancel. This active-orders path is the gap.

critic.title: Scoped TP freeze misses scanner-withheld conflicts: a cell whose committed fill is contradicted still gets a new TP from that quantity
critic.requirement: NG-HIST-002 / AC-40: one key with a different payload is a history conflict and pauses; quantity is never guessed. NG-OPS-001: an unknown fill blocks new exposure of the affected cell. The review fix #2 (trace ws-d-engine.md row 2) limits TP blocking to the affected cells via `tp_blocked_cells`.
critic.failure_scenario: Two review fixes combine badly. (1) The history scanner now withholds conflicted keys (history.py:658-667), so the store never records them. (2) `_scoped_tp_blocks` only blocks TPs for cells named by a store `open_conflicts` row with a CID. A payload or committed-payload conflict on an own trade therefore never names its cell. Walk-through: entry fill T1=3 is committed, and the TP is held below the 5 LIT floor. The venue then re-serves T1 with size 1, which is a `committed_payload_mismatch`. The engine goes FROZEN, but `tp_blocked_cells=={}` and there are no store conflicts. A further fill of 2 makes the committed E=5, and a TP of 5 is dispatched and goes LIVE. That TP is built from the contradicted 3. If the venue's corrected value is true, the TP over-closes the cell by 2 LIT and creates unintended net exposure, while the engine reports FROZEN. The store headroom check does not help because it uses the committed E=5.
critic.evidence: Scratch probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikhail/ed31a3df-55bd-475b-8111-912d06f80d1d/scratchpad/verify/test_probe_ack_conflict.py::test_probe_tp_dispatched_for_cell_with_contradicted_fill prints: `after conflict: EngineState.FROZEN [... 'STORE:manual reconciliation required: history conflict: conflict:committed_payload_mismatch:...']`, `tp_blocked_cells: {} open store conflicts: []`, `E: 5 TPs: [(1099511627787, '5', 'LIVE')] state: EngineState.FROZEN`, `cell blocker: None`. `_scoped_tp_blocks` (engine.py:1928-1941) iterates only `self.open_conflicts` (store rows). `_apply_history` (engine.py ~1580) turns scanner conflicts only into `mark_manual_reconcile_required`, with no cell or CID mapping, even though the withheld row carries `own_client_order_id`.

critic.title: Operator ack_history_conflict cannot restore history completeness for payload conflicts; the grid stays RECONCILING forever and STOP ends STOP_UNCERTAIN
critic.requirement: NG-HIST-002 / AC-40 / AC-12: a conflict pauses until an operator audit. The web offers `ack_history_conflict` as that audit, and `_acknowledge_scan_conflicts` documents that audited conflicts 'are not re-flagged, and the walk boundary is rebased'. NG-OPS-003: stop must be able to finish once own orders are terminal.
critic.failure_scenario: The venue keeps serving an own trade or order row whose payload differs from the committed one, e.g. a changed field (`committed_payload_mismatch`) or a duplicate with another payload. The operator audits it with `ack_history_conflict`, which is APPLIED. `_only_audited_conflicts` converts a walk to complete only when every conflict starts with `conflict:trades_exceed_order_cumulative:`, so every later walk stays `complete=False` / `conflict`. Rebasing the floor to now-overlap does not help. `_fetch_page` (history.py:602-605) applies every row of a page, including rows older than the boundary, so the contradicted row keeps conflicting while it is within the first 100 rows. On a low-volume grid that is indefinitely. The results: history_complete stays False, so no leg settles and no cell releases; entries stay blocked with HISTORY_INCOMPLETE; a venue-cancelled partially filled entry stays TERMINAL_UNKNOWN; a STOP can only end STOP_UNCERTAIN. No other audit action lifts this.
critic.evidence: Probe test_probe_ack_conflict.py::test_probe_committed_payload_mismatch_after_ack (same scratch dir). After an APPLIED ack (`{'status': 'APPLIED', 'result': {'resolved_conflicts': []}}`) and 600 ticks it prints `last: (599, 'RECONCILING', False, 'conflict')` and `walk conflicts: ['conflict:committed_payload_mismatch:...']`. After a venue cancel it prints `entry after venue cancel: TERMINAL_UNKNOWN 2 history_complete False`, and after STOP `stop outcome: STOP_UNCERTAIN`. The sibling probe test_probe_persistent_payload_conflict_after_ack shows the same for `duplicate_key_payload_mismatch`. Code: engine.py:1449-1465 (kind whitelist), engine.py:1072-1082 (ack only rebases the floor), history.py:602-615.

critic.title: Launcher START that turns CONFLICT is silently dropped; an explicit resume-after-stop phrase has no effect
critic.requirement: Review fix A/B and NG-OPS-003 / AC-36: a durable stop may be resumed only by an explicit operator START or a launcher resume naming that stop. Operator commands must reflect committed state, and a refused start must be visible (`start_error`).
critic.failure_scenario: The executor enqueues the launcher START (with `resume_stop_ms`) in `on_start` using the current revisions. An older queued command, for example a PAUSE clicked in the attach-mode web UI while Hummingbot was down, is claimed first in the same tick and APPLIED, which bumps `engine_revision`. `claim_next_command` then marks the launcher START as CONFLICT (`stale_at_apply`). `_track_start` only reacts to REJECTED. Review fix A made `_track_stop` re-send a CONFLICTed STOP, and `_maybe_migrate` / `_maybe_confirm_baseline` retry too, but START was not given the same handling. The START is never re-sent and `start_error` stays None, so the engine silently stays STOPPED although the operator typed the exact resume phrase for that stop.

critic.title: Executor forwards every connector fill as a WS trade hint; fills outside this market never clear, so lag grows forever and baseline audits are refused
critic.requirement: AC-13: history lag must be shown honestly. AC-30 / NG-RISK-003: a baseline audit or rebase must stay possible. Review fix D refuses the audit while any WS trade signal is pending.
critic.failure_scenario: ExecutorBase registers the fill forwarder on the whole connector, so `process_order_filled_event` fires for every order of that connector. `_wake` forwards each one without checking `event.trading_pair` or whether `event.order_id` is a grid CID. `engine.wake` stores the trade id in `ws_pending`, and it is removed only when that trade id is committed from this market's history. Trade labels are never pruned by complete walks. Any fill of another market on the same connector therefore stays pending forever, for example another V2 controller using this generic controller's connector. `history_lag_s` then grows without bound (a false AC-13 lag in snapshot, UI and CLI). `_audit_evidence_unsettled` (engine.py:1061) makes every `baseline` audit REJECTED with `AUDIT_EVIDENCE_NOT_SETTLED`, so after drift the operator can never rebase.

Code: executor.py:357-365 has no filter; engine.py:665-684 is `ws_pending.setdefault`; engine.py:1437-1438 prunes only non-trade labels; executor_base.py:59/329-335 subscribes on the whole connector.

critic.title: Launcher pre-start ledger reads fail on an older schema: the resume phrase is ignored and CID pre-registration is skipped

critic.failure_scenario: The example says `default is <hummingbot data path>/neutral_grid_<grid_id>.sqlite`.
